systems.name: Frame & fork
systems.description: A step-through frame whose down tube sweeps low to the bottom bracket, so there is no top tube to swing a leg over. The fork, fenders, rear rack and kickstand all attach to it.
systems.principle: With no top tube, the wide down tube carries most of the load and doubles as the battery mount. The chain stays and seat stays form a stiff rear triangle that holds the rear wheel and motor.

systems.name: Cockpit & saddle
systems.description: A swept-back handlebar for an upright position, two brake levers, a small central display and a wide saddle on a height-adjustable seatpost.
systems.principle: The display shows speed, charge and assist level; the rider picks the assist level with buttons. Each brake lever has a switch that tells the controller to cut the motor the moment it is pulled.

systems.name: Lithium-ion battery
systems.description: The pack sits on the down tube and lifts off so it can be charged indoors. Inside, thumb-sized 18650 cells are stacked into a block with a protective BMS board.
systems.principle: Ten cells in series raise the voltage to 36 V and three parallel strings add capacity: a 10S3P pack of 30 cells. The BMS balances the cells and disconnects on over-current, over-temperature or deep discharge.

systems.name: Motor & drivetrain
systems.description: The motor is built into the rear hub. A controller under the frame takes power from the battery and feeds the motor. The rider still pedals normally through cranks, chainring, chain and cog.
systems.principle: A pedal-assist sensor (PAS) tells the controller the rider is pedalling; the controller drives current through the stator windings and the magnetic field spins the magnet-lined motor shell together with the wheel. In Vietnam, e-bikes are limited to a design speed of 25 km/h.

systems.name: Wheels
systems.description: Two 26-inch wheels with 2.0-inch tyres, wide enough to soften rough streets. Each wheel has 32 spokes tensioned between rim and hub; the rear wheel uses the motor as its hub.
systems.principle: Spokes work in tension: the load hangs the hub from the rim through the upper spokes. Crossed lacing lets the spokes transmit motor torque and braking force as well.

systems.name: Disc brakes
systems.description: Disc brakes on both wheels: a steel rotor bolted to the hub and a caliper that clamps it when the lever is pulled. E-bikes are heavier and faster than ordinary bicycles, so they need stronger brakes.
systems.principle: Pulling the lever tensions the cable, the caliper presses two pads against the rotor and turns motion into heat. At the same time the switch in the lever cuts motor power so the motor never pushes against the brakes.

pieces.frame.head: The head tube holds the steerer and headset bearings; the handlebar turns around this axis.
pieces.frame.down: The curved down tube is the backbone of the step-through frame: it joins the head tube to the bottom bracket and carries the battery.
pieces.frame.seat: The seat tube holds the seatpost and anchors the seat stays.
pieces.frame.bb: The bottom bracket shell houses the bearings of the crank axle.
pieces.stay.chain: The chain stay joins the bottom bracket to the rear axle and resists the chain’s pull.
pieces.stay.seat: The seat stay joins the seat tube to the rear axle, closing a stiff rear triangle with the chain stay.
pieces.fork.crown: The fork crown joins both fork legs to the steerer that runs through the head tube.
pieces.fork.leg: The fork leg holds the front axle. Its forward curve (rake) helps the bike keep itself straight.
pieces.fender: The fender stops water and mud spraying onto the rider and the battery.
pieces.rack: The rear rack carries bags or a basket; on many models the battery sits here instead of on the down tube.
pieces.kickstand: A side kickstand that keeps the bike upright when parked.
pieces.stem: The stem joins the steerer to the handlebar and sets reach and bar height.
pieces.handlebar: A swept-back handlebar for a relaxed, upright riding position.
pieces.grip: A rubber grip. On many e-bikes the right grip is a twist throttle or carries assist buttons.
pieces.brake.lever: The brake lever pulls the brake cable; a switch inside tells the controller to cut the motor.
pieces.display: The display shows speed, charge, distance and the selected assist level.
pieces.saddle: A wide saddle with a broad rear for upright riding.
pieces.seatpost: The seatpost slides in the seat tube to set saddle height for the rider.
pieces.battery.case: An impact-resistant casing with a lock and charging port; it lifts off for indoor charging.
pieces.battery.cells: Lithium-ion 18650 cells arranged 10 in series × 3 in parallel (10S3P) for 36 V. Simplified: the BMS board and nickel strips are not drawn.
pieces.motor.hub: The motor shell carries permanent magnets and turns with the wheel; the spokes attach directly to it.
pieces.motor.stator: The stator is fixed to the axle and wound with copper coils. The controller switches current through them, creating a rotating field that drags the shell around.
pieces.controller: The controller reads the pedal sensor, brake levers and display, then meters current from battery to motor.
pieces.cable: Cables from battery to controller and controller to motor (orange so they stand out in the model).
pieces.bb.axle: The axle through the bottom bracket that joins both cranks. The pedal-assist sensor usually sits here.
pieces.crank: The crank arm carries leg force from the pedal into the axle.
pieces.pedal: The pedal, where the foot pushes down on the crank.
pieces.chainring: The front chainring turns with the cranks and pulls the chain.
pieces.chain: The chain carries pedalling force from the chainring to the rear cog.
pieces.cog: The rear cog takes the chain’s pull and turns the wheel through a one-way freewheel.
pieces.spokes: Spokes tensioned between rim and hub; the wheel stays true because of that tension.
pieces.hub: The front hub contains the bearings and axle of the front wheel.
pieces.tire: A 26 × 2.0-inch tyre: wide enough for comfort and grip on city streets.
pieces.rim: The aluminium rim holds the tyre and anchors the outer end of each spoke.
pieces.disc: A 160 mm steel brake rotor bolted to the hub, turning with the wheel.
pieces.caliper: The caliper clamps two pads onto the rotor when the lever is pulled.

notes: An illustrative model, not a real product: the shape is built entirely in code (scripts/procedural/ebike.mjs) and the figures are typical values for a city e-bike.
